title: Etale space isomorphisms are detected on a thickening
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme and let $f:V\to W$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose $f$ is chartwise etale in the sense of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]: its composite with every representable etale scheme chart of $V$ is representable etale. Let $i:W_0\hookrightarrow W$ be a thickening, meaning a representable closed immersion whose scheme base changes are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] and which induces a homeomorphism on underlying spaces, with the quotient topology from a surjective etale scheme atlas. If $$V\times_W W_0\longrightarrow W_0$$ is an isomorphism [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], then $f$ is an isomorphism. No quasi-compactness, separation or finite-order condition is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05ZH, theorem-topological-invariance, applied to the thickening W_0 -> W, and reflection of isomorphisms under its equivalence of categories of etale algebraic spaces. See also Tag 05ZS, lemma-thickening-equivalence, for scheme objects.

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T$ over $B$ and a map $T\to W$. Put $E=V\times_WT$, $T_0=W_0\times_WT$ and $E_0=E\times_TT_0$. These are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The base-change clause of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] makes $g:E\to T$ chartwise etale. Apply [lem-sfb-space-thickening-base-change] to $i$ and $T\to W$: its point classes and atlas topology are exactly the underlying-space convention in the hypothesis. It gives a representable closed immersion $T_0\to T$ inducing a homeomorphism; since $T$ is a scheme, $T_0$ is a scheme as well. Thus $T_0\to T$ is a thickening, with no finite-order condition. The hypothesis identifies $E_0\to T_0$ with an isomorphism: on sections the identification $E_0\simeq (V\times_WW_0)\times_{W_0}T_0$ forgets the repeated $W$-coordinate, with inverse inserting its forced value. In particular no representability of $f$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 05ZH (theorem-topological-invariance), faithfulness/open-equalizer argument specialized to a thickening; Tag 09ZX (lemma-base-change-thickening).

proof.text: For each representable etale scheme chart $A\to E$, the composite $A\to T$ is etale by step 1 and therefore unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. These are precisely the chart hypotheses of [lem-sfb-unramified-space-open-diagonal], whose target $T$ is a scheme. Thus $\delta:E\to D:=E\times_TE$ is a representable open immersion.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), part (1), with scheme target T.

proof.text: Test $\delta$ on an arbitrary scheme $H\to D$. Its pullback is an open subscheme $U\subseteq H$. Set $H_0=H\times_TT_0$; [lem-sfb-space-thickening-base-change] applied to $T_0\to T$ and the composite $H\to D\to T$ makes $H_0\to H$ a representable closed immersion and a homeomorphism on point spaces. In particular $H_0$ is a scheme and this morphism is surjective on scheme points. After this base change, the open immersion $U\to H$ is the pullback of $\delta_0:E_0\to E_0\times_{T_0}E_0$. This is an isomorphism: since $E_0\to T_0$ is an isomorphism, two sections over the same section of $T_0$ coincide; the first projection is the inverse to $\delta_0$. Consequently $U\times_HH_0\to H_0$ is an isomorphism, so $H_0\to H$ factors through $U$. Its surjectivity implies $|U|=|H|$, and the open-subscheme description in [def-weil-open-immersion] gives $U=H$. Hence every scheme test of $\delta$ is an isomorphism. Equivalently, for each test scheme $H$ and pair $(a,b)\in D(H)$ there is exactly one section of $E(H)$ mapping to $(a,b)$; these inverses commute with restrictions by uniqueness. Thus $\delta$ itself is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05ZH (theorem-topological-invariance), faithfulness/open-equalizer argument specialized to a thickening; Tag 09ZX (lemma-base-change-thickening).

proof.text: For any test scheme $H$ and $a,b\in E(H)$ with $g(a)=g(b)$, the pair $(a,b)$ belongs to $D(H)$. Surjectivity of $\delta_H$ from step 3 gives a section $c$ with $(a,b)=(c,c)$, so $a=b$. Thus $g$ is a monomorphism of sheaves. Together with the chartwise etaleness from step 1 this supplies both hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open], applied over $B$. It follows that $g:E\to T$ is representable by open immersions.

Testing the open immersion $g$ on $\operatorname{id}_T$ identifies $E$ over $T$ with an open subscheme $O\subseteq T$. The isomorphism $E_0\to T_0$ of step 1 gives a factorization $T_0\to O\to T$: use its inverse followed by the projection $E_0\to E=O$. Since the thickening $T_0\to T$ is surjective on points, $|O|=|T|$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], an open subscheme with this underlying open is $T$ itself. Hence $g$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05ZH (theorem-topological-invariance), faithfulness/open-equalizer argument specialized to a thickening; Tag 09ZX (lemma-base-change-thickening).

proof.text: The scheme map $T\to W$ in step 1 was arbitrary. Given any $B$-scheme $H$ and section $y\in W(H)$, take $T=H$ with map $y$. The isomorphism $V\times_WH\to H$ of step 5 gives a unique section above $\operatorname{id}_H$, that is, a unique $x\in V(H)$ with $f_H(x)=y$. These bijections are natural: restricting a lift still lifts the restricted section, and uniqueness identifies it with the unique lift of that section. Their inverses therefore define a natural transformation inverse to $f$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space], morphisms of algebraic spaces are natural transformations, so this is an inverse morphism over $B$. Thus $f$ is an isomorphism.
